subject: Emergency data handshake protocol discussion
messages:
From: Tim Walsh <tim.walsh@clearstream.io>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@clearstream.io
Date: Fri, 30 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Request to align emergency access protocol in DPA

Hi Soojin,

I’m reaching out from ClearStream’s security team — we’ve encountered a system event that may require expedited access to provider-side logs and limited packet captures to support our forensic triage. Our SOC is asking for clarity on Redwood’s timelines and mechanism for evidence handoff under the current DPA and whether a temporary expedited path (48h) is possible for critical customers.

Key asks:
- Confirmation of Redwood’s incident notification timeline and whether initial evidence can be made available within 48 hours of request.
- Whether Redwood can provide an SFTP/secure-bucket handoff for forensic artifacts and a named subprocessor contact for any downstream exports.
- Any constraints around cross-border transfer for artifacts that may include E2E headers.

We’ve attached a short incident_summary.pdf with the types of artifacts we’d request. We’d like to avoid engaging full legal redlines unless needed — can your SOC ops liaison and legal provide a short, operational playbook we can rely on while we finalize contractual language?

Thanks — this is time sensitive for our customer.

—Tim
Tim Walsh
Head of Security, ClearStream

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Urgent: Request to align emergency access protocol in DPA

Tim —

Thanks for the heads-up and for the incident summary. I’ve looped in Ben (sales lead) and Kimberly (privacy & legal) so we can coordinate both the operational handoff and any limited contractual adjustments. Quick operational notes from our side:

- Standard Redwood DPA: we provide incident notification to affected customers and relevant contacts within a 72-hour window after confirming material impact.
- Operational compromise: for high-severity events we can initiate an expedited evidence intake process and make a modest set of artifacts available via a security-tier S3 bucket/SFTP within ~48 hours, subject to legal review and export controls.
- Subprocessor access: Redwood’s subprocessors do not get direct access to customer artifacts unless both parties authorize. We will provide a named contact for our infra subprocessor if chains of custody require it.

I’m attaching a very short draft_snippet (draft_emergency_clause_redline.docx) that sketches an "emergency data handshake" — it is explicitly narrow: initial evidence intake, chain-of-custody controls, retention window, and an audit log requirement. This is intended to be an operational bridge while legal works on an amendment.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to review and propose minimal legal language (I’ll give her context).
2) Confirm who at ClearStream will receive and store artifacts (SOP + contact).
3) Sched a 30m sync early next week to align process and timelines.

If ClearStream needs a 48-hour guarantee for the initial intake, we can consider a one-off SLA exception for the affected account pending executed amendment.

Sooj in
Soojin Lee
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Urgent: Request to align emergency access protocol in DPA

Tim and team —

Thanks for raising this. Operationally we’re sympathetic to ClearStream’s needs; legally we need to preserve both customer data protections and Redwood’s obligations to subprocessors and export rules. Below is proposed language and process elements we can accept as an interim operational runway. Please treat as draft for redline.

Proposed interim protocol (high level):
- Notification vs. evidence: Redwood will issue incident notification within 72 hours of confirmation; initial evidence intake (limited logs, session metadata, and relevant packet headers) may be staged for customer retrieval within 48 hours where the customer’s security team demonstrates a legitimate investigatory need.
- Authorization: Evidence retrieval requires an authorized request from a named security contact and a retrieval affidavit. Requests must be logged with chain-of-custody metadata.
- Subprocessor coordination: If evidence involves a subprocessor, Redwood will: (a) notify the customer that a subprocessor is involved; (b) provide the subprocessor’s designated liaison; and (c) coordinate the transfer under the same chain-of-custody process.
- Cross-border considerations: Any artifacts that include PII or payloads that implicate transfer restrictions will be redacted or subject to an export-control review before transfer. If export controls block transfer, Redwood will provide a detailed summary of the artifacts and offer in-place analysis options (redacted or under an approved remote session with Redwood engineers).
- Retention and scope: Staged artifacts will be retained for 90 days from handoff unless the customer requests extended custody in writing.

Operational requirements and minimal assurances:
- Secure handoff via pre-provisioned S3 with SSE-KMS or SFTP to customer-controlled endpoint.
- Full access/audit logs accompany every handoff.
- Redwood reserves the right to refuse requests that exceed scope or are inconsistent with the DPA without a signed amendment.

If ClearStream agrees in principle, legal can produce a short amendment (1–2 paragraphs) to the DPA that references an "Emergency Evidence Handoff" protocol and enumerates the steps above. I can push a redline today; please confirm what ClearStream needs in the amendment (e.g., guaranteed 48-hour SLA vs. best-effort plus escalation path).

I’m CC’ing Marissa from Support Ops so we can draft the SOP for the actual handoff process (S3 bucket naming, pre-signed URL cadence, expiration, encryption profile).

Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy & Legal — Redwood Inference

Kimberly / Soojin —

Appreciate the thorough and pragmatic draft. ClearStream accepts the interim approach in principle. A few clarifications before we sign off:

1) Proof-of-process: can Redwood share the SOP (S3 naming, rotation, KMS key id, audit log sample) so we can validate against our internal chain-of-custody requirements?
2) SLA ask: We’d like an explicit 48-hour initial evidence intake guarantee for this affected account (temporary SLA exception) until the amendment is executed. If Redwood can commit to that for the customer, we’ll take the amendment to legal and DocuSign.
3) Canary: would Redwood be willing to run a one-off dry-run (transfer a small synthetic artifact) to validate the end-to-end flow before we need artifacts forensics?

If you can provide the SOP and the draft amendment link we’ll route through our counsel. Proposed quick sync: Tue 02 Apr 2028 09:00 PT — ok for you?

Attaching our evidence intake template for your SOP mapping.

Thanks,

—Tim
Tim Walsh
